ExceptionHandling.// IncludeDetails: Explicit false: the E2E suite runs in Development, and the hardened error shape is what must be assertable there.

JwtBearer.// RequireAuthenticatedEndpoints: false is #5's documented whole-application opt-out: the 28 pre-existing anonymous E2E tests stay green, and exactly one endpoint opts back in with [Authorize] (the #9 demo).

ClientCredentials.// ClientSecret: An obvious placeholder for the local-only test identity provider the E2E fixture hosts on 5310 — never a real credential. Real secrets come from KeyVault / environment / user-secrets, never appsettings.json.

OpenIdConnect.// ClientSecret: An obvious placeholder for the local-only test identity provider the E2E fixture hosts on 5310 — never a real credential. Real secrets come from KeyVault / environment / user-secrets, never appsettings.json.
OpenIdConnect.// RequireAuthenticatedEndpoints: false is D-6's documented whole-application opt-out: the 31 pre-existing anonymous E2E tests stay green, and the #10 user endpoints opt back in with [Authorize]. The Cookie settings stay at their D-1 defaults on purpose, so the E2E run proves __Host-/Secure cookies work in Chromium on loopback.

UserApi.//: The #10 demo client: both flags on one client — the signed-in user's token is the one that reaches the peer (AC-CC13 live).
